subject: Midterm capacity increase and billing ask
messages:
From: Sage Morales <sage@novalytics.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Daniel Cho <daniel.cho@novalytics.com>
Date: Sun, 10 Jan 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Midterm capacity bump — pro-rate + co-term question

Hi Jordan,

We're planning to accelerate a portion of our roadmap and expect usage to grow from ~2M tokens/month to ~3.5M tokens/month starting Feb 1. This is a midterm uplift on our current contract (annual, co-term to Jun 30). Two asks: can Redwood provide (1) a pro-rated billing approach for Feb–Jun and (2) a path to align this additional capacity with our existing Jun 30 co-term (we'd prefer not to open a separate 12 month contract).

We attached a short note that outlines expected monthly volumes and timing. From a commercial perspective, Novalytics is looking for a modest uplift discount on the incremental commit — something in the range of 8–12% would make this workable for internal approval. If there's an alternative structure that avoids starting a new 12 month term (e.g., temporary uplift through co-term with a one-time credit), we'd be open to that.

Can you confirm what options you can provide and any turnaround on pricing? We need internal sign-off by Jan 22 to make the Feb 1 start.

Thanks,
Sage
Sage Morales
Head of Platform
Novalytics

Attachment: Novalytics_MPL_Uplift_Request_2027.pdf (summary of expected volumes and preferred timing)

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Sage Morales <sage@novalytics.com>
Cc: Daniel Cho <daniel.cho@novalytics.com>
Date: Sun, 10 Jan 2027 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Midterm capacity bump — pro-rate + co-term question

Hi Sage — thanks for the note and the timing context. This is doable; appreciate the target (Feb 1 start and sign-off by Jan 22). A couple quick clarifying Qs so I give you precise options:

- Is the 3.5M token/month commitment expected to be steady through Jun 30, or is there a taper afterwards?
- Is Novalytics willing to take a short committed uplift (Feb–Jun) in exchange for a one-time credit or would you prefer an extended co-term through Dec 31?

I'll loop in finance and my manager to get formal pricing options and a short proposal PDF you can present. Aim to get you two clean options (short-term pro-rate vs co-term commit) by early next week.

Appreciate the timeline — I'll be back with numbers.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 11 Jan 2027 09:00:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Novalytics capacity ask — pricing guidance needed

Laura / Marcus — forwarding Novalytics' ask below. They want to increase from 2M -> 3.5M tokens/month starting Feb 1, and prefer to keep everything co-term to Jun 30. They are asking for an 8–12% uplift discount on the incremental commit.

Key constraints: sign-off by Jan 22. Options I'm thinking we can present:

Option A (short-term uplift): Feb–Jun billed at standard list rate on the incremental usage, with a one-time pro-rated credit applied to the Feb invoice to reflect partial-term concession. Easier operationally, lower discount.

Option B (commit to co-term through Jun 30 with an agreed uplift rebate): Novalytics commits to the higher monthly baseline through Jun 30; we apply a modest percentage discount on the incremental tokens and amortize a credit across Feb–Jun. This avoids a new 12 month term.

Can you run a quick P&L for both options and indicate what level of discount we can approve at director level vs require CRO sign-off? I'm attaching a blank proposal template to fill.

Thanks — Jordan

Attachment: Redwood-Proposal-blank.xlsx

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 13 Jan 2027 14:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Novalytics capacity ask — pricing guidance needed

Jordan / Laura,

Ran-through the numbers based on their ask (Feb 1 start, incremental 1.5M tokens/month). Below are two commercially viable options — both assume current list pricing for base consumption and apply concessions only to the incremental uplift: 

Option 1 — Temporary uplift (Feb–Jun):
- Billed at list on incremental volume, one-time pro-rated credit applied to Feb invoice: $12,500 credit (handles partial-month and operational smoothing).
- Total incremental revenue Feb–Jun: $225,000 before credit.
- Approval: OK at director level (Laura). No CRO approval needed.

Option 2 — Co-term commit (Feb–Jun elevated baseline, avoid new 12mo):
- Customer commits to elevated baseline through Jun 30; we provide a 12% discount on incremental tokens for Feb–Jun and amortize a $30,000 credit across invoices to reflect partial-year concession.
- Effective incremental revenue Feb–Jun: $198,000.
- Approval: requires CRO approval if discount >12%; 12% is the max we can approve today at director level.

If they prefer to co-term through Dec 31 or roll the uplift into a new 12 month term, we can offer more aggressive pricing but that changes the ask.

Attaching a filled proposal draft for Option 2 with line-item math. If Laura signs off on Option 2 at 12%, I'll prepare the DocuSign and finalize the invoice schedule.

Marcus
Finance — Revenue Operations

Attachment: Redwood-Proposal-2027-v2.xlsx

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Sage Morales <sage@novalytics.com>, Daniel Cho <daniel.cho@novalytics.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 18 Jan 2027 16:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Midterm capacity bump — proposal and next steps

Hi Sage / Daniel — thanks for the patience. Per our internal review we can present two options that align with your timeline: 

Option A — Temporary uplift (Feb 1 through Jun 30):
- Incremental 1.5M tokens/month billed at list.
- One-time pro-rated operational credit applied to Feb invoice: $12,500.
- No change to current contract term; easiest operational path.

Option B — Co-term elevated baseline through Jun 30 (no new 12mo):
- Customer commits to elevated baseline through Jun 30. We apply a 12% discount on incremental tokens (max approvable at director level) and amortize a $30,000 credit across Feb–Jun invoices.
- This meets your ask to avoid a separate 12 month agreement while giving a modest commercial concession.

Attached is the proposal spreadsheet with line-item math and the DocuSign link to accept Option B if you'd like to proceed that way. If you want a slightly more aggressive % we can explore extending the term (Dec 31 or 12 months) but that will need CRO review.

Next steps:
1) Pick Option A or B and confirm by Jan 22 to hit Feb 1 start.
2) If Option B, I'll send the DocuSign for signature and confirm invoice schedule.

Thanks — happy to jump on a 20 minute call if you want to walk through the numbers.

Best,
Jordan Blake
